transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Um… I guess what finally pushed me to come in is work. I’m a medical services manager, and I’ll sit down to start an EPIC quality report or be in a clinic metrics meeting really trying to follow everything, and then a few minutes later I realize my mind has just… gone somewhere else completely. Like I’m rereading the same numbers over and over, or I’ve missed the whole point of what someone was saying. It’s frustrating, because I meant to pay attention.
Thinking back, would you say you've had this kind of trouble focusing since you were a child, or is this something that's developed more recently, say in the past several months?

No, it’s definitely not just the last few months. I mean, it feels worse now because work is more complicated, but thinking back… even in elementary school, teachers would write things like, “She’s bright but careless,” which I always hated because it sounded like I wasn’t trying.

My mom used to have to sit with me while I did homework, not because I couldn’t understand it, but because I’d just lose track of what I was supposed to be doing. Or I’d realize I’d left the book I needed at school. I remember this one little desk we had in the kitchen—actually, it was by the phone, back when we had the long curly cord—and she’d be cooking dinner and reminding me, “Okay, finish the next problem.” So… yes, it goes way back.
Do you often feel excessively sleepy during the day, even after what seems like a full night's sleep, to the point that it's hard to stay awake or alert?

I’m not totally sure. I don’t think I’m, like, falling asleep during the day or fighting to keep my eyes open in meetings. I mean, I get tired like anyone does—especially depending on the week, and honestly the lighting in some conference rooms is awful, that sort of humming fluorescent thing—but I wouldn’t say it feels like sleepiness exactly. More like my attention just slips off.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling persistently down, sad, or losing interest in things you'd normally enjoy?

Um… I don’t know. I wouldn’t say I’ve been persistently sad, exactly. Like, I get frustrated with myself, especially when I feel like I’m not keeping up, but I don’t think it’s a constant down feeling.

Interest-wise… I mean, I still enjoy things when I can actually settle into them. Although that’s the part where I get annoyed, because I’ll start something—like I have this half-finished organizing project in the hall closet from, I think, two weekends ago, and then I found old photos in there and suddenly that became the whole afternoon. But no, I don’t think I’ve lost interest in everything or anything like that.
Do you often find yourself feeling restless, fidgety, or having trouble sitting still, or acting impulsively—like interrupting others or making quick decisions without thinking them through?

Hmm… I’m not sure. Restless maybe sometimes, but I don’t think of myself as someone who can’t sit still. I’ll shift around in a chair or mess with a pen if I’m in a long meeting, but honestly half the time I’m also thinking about, like, whether I answered that email from the lab director—or no, not the lab director, the operations person—anyway.

Interrupting… I hope not? I mean, I probably do jump in when I’m worried I’ll forget what I was going to say, but I don’t know if that’s “impulsive” exactly. Quick decisions… I can be a little spontaneous with small stuff, like buying some organizing bins and then realizing they don’t fit the shelf, which is ridiculous because I could’ve measured it. But big decisions, I usually overthink. So I guess… not really in a major way?
Aside from work, do these attention and focus problems also cause noticeable difficulties in other areas of your life—like managing things at home, in relationships, or with daily responsibilities?

Yeah, it’s not just work, though work is where it’s most obvious because there are deadlines and other people can see it. My delays have started affecting clinic reporting deadlines, and then other teams are sort of waiting on me, which feels awful.

Outside of that… I used to help lead parts of these volunteer health workshops, and I’ve had to step back from some of that because I just can’t reliably keep all the planning pieces moving. Like the sign-ups, materials, who’s bringing what—well, I guess that is kind of work-adjacent because it’s health-related, but it’s not my job. I’d mean to follow up and then realize too late that I hadn’t, so I stopped taking the lead on those parts.
Do you often lose or misplace things you need, like your keys, phone, or important paperwork, or forget appointments and commitments in your daily life?

Yes—unfortunately, yes. I’m constantly hunting for things I need, like my badge, handwritten notes, clinic folders… even a flash drive I swear I just had in my hand before a meeting.

And then I’ll be digging through my bag or checking the same stack of papers three times, and it’s embarrassing because I used to be the organized one. I was the person other people asked where things were. Now I’ll be standing there thinking, “How did I lose this between my desk and the conference room?”
Do you often find yourself worrying excessively about different things—like work performance, health, or other everyday matters—more than you feel you should?

I mean… I worry about things, sure, but I don’t know if I’d call it excessive. Work stuff gets in my head, especially if I think I’ve missed something or someone’s waiting on me, but then sometimes I’m also thinking about totally random things like whether I left the laundry in the washer or if I need to pick up coffee filters—sorry, that’s not really what you asked.

I guess I’m not sure where the line is between normal worrying and too much worrying. I don’t feel like I’m constantly panicked about everything, if that’s what you mean. It’s more like certain things nag at me, and then my mind jumps around.
Have you ever had a period lasting several days where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or needed much less sleep than usual, along with being more talkative or impulsive than normal?

Um… I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had stretches where I stayed up too late or felt kind of keyed up if there was a big deadline or something going on, but not like several days where I felt unusually elated or like I didn’t need sleep.

I can be talkative when I’m nervous—actually my sister says I explain things in circles, which is probably true—but I wouldn’t say I’ve had a period where I was more impulsive than normal in that way. I guess I’d say no, not that I’ve noticed.

Between childhood and now, was there ever a stretch of time—like in high school, college, or early in your career—when these attention and organization problems weren't really a issue for you, or has it been fairly consistent the whole way through?

I don’t think there was ever a totally clean stretch where it wasn’t an issue. I mean, it looked different at different ages, but… even in elementary school, I remember teachers writing things like that I was bright but careless.

My mom had to sit with me while I did homework, not because I couldn’t understand it, but because I’d lose track of what I was supposed to be doing, or I’d forget the book I needed at school. Which is funny—not funny, but… I can still picture her at the kitchen table trying to keep me on task while dinner was going, and I’d be digging through my backpack insisting the worksheet had to be in there.

So I guess, no, it hasn’t just been recent. It’s been kind of woven through the whole way, even if I managed around it better sometimes.

Which is funny—not funny, but… I can still picture her at the kitchen table trying to keep me on task while dinner was going, and I’d be digging through my backpack insisting the worksheet had to be in there.

So I guess, no, it hasn’t just been recent. It’s been kind of woven through the whole way, even if I managed around it better sometimes.
